name: Coronation of Manuel II Palaiologos
summary: Manuel II is crowned in Hagia Sophia, succeeding his father John V as Byzantine emperor of a state reduced to Constantinople, Thessalonica, and the Despotate of the Morea. Within months he is fighting alongside Sultan Bayezid I as a tributary vassal.

_quarry.structural_significance: Marks the lowest political ebb of the Byzantine state before its fall in 1453. Manuel's later European tour (1399–1403) to seek military aid is the first time a sitting Byzantine emperor personally crosses the Latin West.
